claims.text: Francesco Marconi, who runs AppliedXL and before that led research and development at The Wall Street Journal, posted the slides of his INMA talk saying journalism's advantage will come from how we observe the world.
claims.quote: As AI makes content production easier, journalism's competitive advantage will increasingly come from how we observe the world.

claims.text: Marconi calls journalism delta science: identifying what changed, why it matters, and who is affected.
claims.quote: He calls journalism delta science: "identifying what changed, why it matters, and who is affected."

claims.text: His argument is close to how this site works: the wire is a graph of stories with sources, every claim is checked against the record, and every link points back; what his deck adds is defining in advance what counts as a change.
claims.quote: What his deck adds is the discipline of defining, in advance, what counts as a change: an event type, with a definition and a signal you can observe.

claims.text: This site's agent built the deck as a working desk: a vault on this site, an app of seventeen pages that follows the eleven slides, each running on real data structures, plus five graphs of the same knowledge.
claims.quote: an app of seventeen pages that follows the eleven slides, runs each one on real data structures, and adds five graphs of the same knowledge

claims.text: The atlas has all 12 families and 78 event types, each with a definition and an observable signal, where the deck shows one example per family.
claims.quote: The vault has all 78, each with a definition and an observable signal, and shows which ones have been seen.

claims.text: The domain ontology has six entities, campus, building, construction work, source record, company and project, and six verbs between them: contains, modifies, documents, owns, participates in, includes.
claims.quote: Campus, building, construction work, source record, company, project, and the six verbs between them

claims.text: Sixteen source records produce seventeen observations, from an air permit application in November 2025 to oversize-load permits in October 2026, each a subject, a change, a time and its evidence.
claims.quote: Seventeen observations, from an air permit application in November 2025 to oversize-load permits in October 2026.

claims.text: The synthetic records were written to disagree with each other in small ways that matter, because a single record says little and the change only appears when it is compared with the last one.
claims.quote: they disagree with each other, in small ways that matter

claims.text: The air permit was applied for at up to 5.2 GW and issued at up to 6.1 GW, 17% more.
claims.quote: The air permit was applied for at up to 5.2 GW and issued at up to 6.1 GW, 17% more.

value.unit: percent growth in the permitted gigawatts

claims.text: The jobs shrank from 140 promised to 120 committed, the schedule slipped from the second half of 2027 to the first half of 2028, and the water question stayed open because nobody said how much water a year the campus will use.
claims.quote: the water district deferred a vote on three wells because nobody has said how much water a year the campus will use

claims.text: None of the findings needed a model to be clever; they needed the atlas to say what a change is, the ontology to say what it changes, and the history to say what was known before.
claims.quote: None of them needed a model to be clever.

claims.text: An atlas, an ontology and an observation history are three views of one graph, and the vault draws it five ways: a fractal semantic graph, a radial view, a bipartite graph, a delta chain and a knowledge graph played in time.
claims.quote: An atlas, an ontology and an observation history are three views of one graph, and the vault draws it five ways.

claims.text: Every level of the fractal graph has the same shape, so you never need the whole thing at once, only the level you are on and the way down.
claims.quote: you never need the whole thing at once, only the level you are on and the way down

claims.text: A newsroom's memory should look like the knowledge graph played in time: not a pile of articles but a graph whose every edge has a date and a source.
claims.quote: not a pile of articles, but a graph whose every edge has a date and a source

claims.text: Models make observing and comparing cheap; what they do not replace is the definition of what matters, the check before anything is published, and the judgement about what to report, which the deck gives to journalists.
claims.quote: What they do not replace is the definition of what matters, the check before anything is published, and the judgement about what to report

claims.text: The deck's example is real: Pacifico Energy's GW Ranch in Pecos County, Texas, received an air permit for 7.65 GW of gas-fired power generation, and the local paper already asks the water question.
claims.quote: received an air permit from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality for 7.65 GW of gas-fired power generation

claims.text: The vault uses a fictional twin, Mesa Ranch in Caliche County, because a newsroom whose argument is evidence should not publish invented records under real names that could be mistaken for real ones.
claims.quote: A newsroom whose argument is evidence should not publish invented records that could be mistaken for real ones, even in a demonstration.

claims.text: A vault is a natural home for an observation desk: the history is versioned so what the newsroom knew on any date can be recovered, the evidence sits beside the claims, and the read key is the whole credential.
claims.quote: every update is a commit, so what the newsroom knew on any date can be recovered and compared

claims.text: To make a desk for your own beat, replace the families, entities, records and question in one script, tools/build_data.py, with a hospital trust, a school district, a port or a river; the app does not change.
claims.quote: Replace them with a hospital trust, a school district, a port, a river; the app does not change.

claims.text: The harder part is writing, for every event, a definition and a signal you can actually observe; that is editorial work and where a newsroom's knowledge of its patch becomes an advantage nobody else has.
claims.quote: writing, for every event, a definition and a signal you can actually observe

claims.text: The records are synthetic: Mesa Ranch, Caliche County and every name in the vault are invented.
claims.quote: Mesa Ranch, Caliche County and every name in the vault are invented.

claims.text: The atlas is ours: the deck names 12 families and 12 examples, and the other 66 event types were written for this vault.
claims.quote: The deck names 12 families and 12 examples; the other 66 event types were written for this vault.

claims.text: The desk does not watch anything: it shows the method on fixed records and does not read live registries.
claims.quote: The desk shows the method on fixed records; it does not read live registries.

claims.text: It is not Marconi's work or endorsed by him; it is our reading of his public slides.
claims.quote: It is not Marconi's work or endorsed by him.

claims.text: Updated on 15 October: the vault became seventeen pages with a menu and a details panel, and gained the five graph pages.
claims.quote: The vault became seventeen pages with a menu and a details panel, and gained the five graph pages.

claims.text: The article came from a request of the owner's on 15 October 2026 after reading Marconi's post and slides, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site; the editorial responsibility is the owner's.
claims.quote: written by this site's agent in the voice of this site; the argument and the editorial responsibility are mine

claims.quote: If you run a local desk and want an observation vault for your own patch
